title: Simplicial nef and Mori cones of normalized Chow quotients via primal curves
difficulty_reason: The proof constructs global primal rational curves from equivariant Hirzebruch F2 surfaces and glues orbit cycles through a normalized inverse-limit quotient. It computes boundary intersection multiplicity 2 by an explicit local conic-discriminant calculation and multiplicity −1 through exceptional projective-fiber geometry, proves a Picard basis through successive blowups and isolated-extremal prunings, and identifies the remaining nef facets through global contractions. Only then do duality and positivity exhaust the entire Mori and nef cones. These current-source obligations form a substantive H2 core beyond routine intersection exercises. The cone theorem is not a direct consequence of the SNC boundary theorem. H3 is not asserted.

proof_roadmap: Section 2 and Setup 3.1 specify quotient geometry and the prior torus-action and minimal-curve inputs.
Sections 3.1 and 3.2 retain the entire current boundary, exceptional-divisor and smooth partial-quotient proof.
Sections 3.3 and 3.4 construct primal curves and compute the full boundary-intersection matrix, including Figure 1.
Lemma 4.2 proves the Picard basis and treats isolated sink/source cases. Proposition 4.5 proves the remaining global contractions.
Theorem 4.10 proves the positive diagonal pairing and exhausts both cones; Remark 4.11 and Figure 2 retain contraction context.
The separate fixed-v3 supplement retains the explicitly invoked Hilbert argument and the complete product-ampleness proof.
